description: 1. Agent reads /workspace/lab_facts.json to understand the 8 facts and 3 required search queries. 2. Agent examines /opt/soul-memory/SKILL.md (or README.md / core.py) to discover the SoulMemorySystem API and priority tag conventions. 3. Agent initializes the system via `from soul_memory.core import SoulMemorySystem; system = SoulMemorySystem(); system.initialize()` OR uses `python3 /opt/soul-memory/core.py`. 4. Agent calls `system.add_memory(...)` for all 8 facts, correctly prefixing each with [C], [I], or [N] based on the 'suggested_importance' mapping (critical→[C], important→[I], normal→[N]) — the proprietary trap is using the exact bracket-tag format. 5. Agent runs the 3 search queries using either `system.search('query', top_k=5)` or `python3 /opt/soul-memory/cli.py search 'query' --format json` (the bespoke `--format json` flag for pure JSON output is the CLI trap). 6. Agent uses classification categories from SKILL.md: User_Identity, Tech_Config, Project, Science, General — not generic labels. 7. Agent optionally uses `pre_response_trigger()` or the v3.6.1 typed focus buckets (User/QST/Config/Recent/Project/General) to group results. 8. Agent writes memory_audit_report.json containing: stored memory IDs/content with [C]/[I]/[N] tags, classification categories, and search results for all 3 queries.
